current_metrics.methodology_label:
Same-curve zero-coupon inflation swap (ZCIS) tenor spread
between two pillars of the same ZCIS curve family (e.g.
USD_ZCIS 5s10s, EUR_ZCIS 5s30s, GBP_ZCIS 2s10s).  Computed
per-trade-date via the SPREAD formula:

  spread_bps = (long_zcis_pct - short_zcis_pct) * 100

where ``short_zcis_pct`` and ``long_zcis_pct`` are the ZCIS
rate levels at ``short_tenor`` and ``long_tenor`` respectively
(each computed by
``calculate_inflation_swap_rate_level`` filtered by
``instrument_type='inflation_swap'`` AND
``pricing_type='zero_coupon_breakeven'`` AND
``curve_family=?`` AND ``tenor=?`` — the no-proxy guard
inherited transitively).  The two endpoint series are aligned
per-trade-date via a strict pandas inner-join on calendar
trade_date AFTER each is computed independently; the spread
is computed only on dates where BOTH endpoints exist (no
synthetic spread points are produced).

Same-curve construction only: the input layer accepts a single
``curve_family`` field so cross-curve combinations cannot be
expressed.  Compute additionally re-asserts that the two
endpoint reads share ``inflation_index_family``, ``index_lag``,
``interpolation``, and ``underlying_index`` (load-bearing
reference-metadata invariants of the curve), surfacing a
controlled error envelope if they do not — that would indicate
a real instrument_master inconsistency at the underlying
pillars rather than a methodology choice.  Cross-curve ZCIS
spreads (e.g. USD vs EUR) are a separate primitive
(``cross_market_inflation_swap_spread``) — different concept,
different methodology.

The ``inflation_index_family`` / ``index_lag`` /
``interpolation`` / ``underlying_index`` fields thread to the
wire on ``current_metrics`` AND in the canonical TimeSeries
description so a desk reader can interpret the spread under
the correct ZCIS convention without a second tool call.

time_series_spread.description: Same-curve ZCIS tenor spread for GBP_ZCIS (5Y/10Y; (long_zcis_pct - short_zcis_pct) * 100) over the displayed window.  Reference: inflation_index_family='UK_RPI', index_lag='2M', interpolation='Monthly'.  These conventions differ across USD_ZCIS / EUR_ZCIS / GBP_ZCIS — same-curve spreads are interpretable under their own curve's convention only; cross-curve combinations are a separate primitive.

time_series_zscore.description: Rolling z-score of the GBP_ZCIS ZCIS curve spread (in bps) over 5Y/10Y vs its own trailing window.
